entities.summary:
Pope Stephen VI, the ruler of the Papal States from 22 May 896 until his death in August 897, is best known for instigating the Cadaver Synod, a pivotal event in the tumultuous history of the Catholic Church. 

    This synod, held in the year 897, was a culmination of the ongoing power struggle between the papacy and the nobility, and its consequences would shape the course of Western Christendom for centuries to come. 

    Through his machinations, Stephen VI inadvertently created a rift between the secular and ecclesiastical powers, paving the way for the eventual decline of the papacy's temporal authority. The long-term effects of this event would be felt across Europe, contributing to the fragmentation of the Holy Roman Empire and the rise of regional nation-states.
